correctness.rationale: Each nonempty partial distance-preserving injection of K_{a,b} has exactly one globally side-preserving or side-exchanging orientation; their only intersection is the empty map. Nilpotents are precisely assemblies of directed paths, giving coefficients x^j u^{j-1}, y^j u^{j-1}, or alternating-color x^{r+1}y^r, x^r y^{r+1}, 2(xy)^r with the prescribed arrow weights. The labeled exponential formula counts them exactly, subtraction of one corrects the zero-map overlap, and successive length cutoffs give exact indices. The independent maximum-index bounds a and 2b+1 (2b balanced), with Hamiltonian-path counts, establish every phase and multiplicity. Standard-library code independently tests all rank/index cells in fifteen labeled small graph configurations. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The nilpotency index and partial-map rank are intrinsic semigroup invariants, and their entire joint polynomial on K_{a,b} is a natural complete counting problem not resolved by known star/cycle cardinality results. Alternating components yield a genuinely new two-color competition with the one-side paths: the exact maximizer changes at a=2b+1, with all extremizer counts explicit. This is a reusable structural and enumerative theorem for arbitrary side sizes, not a tiny finite gain or merely a restatement of the star case.
